data.name: Ilaaf
data.gender_notes: Ilaaf is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'alafa' which means 'to be exalted, to rise up, to ascend'. In Islamic context, the name Ilaaf signifies being lifted up towards the divine and attaining a high spiritual status. The name Ilaaf carries the meaning “Exalted, Sublime” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ilaaf usually hope their child will grow to embody exalted, sublime and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of spiritual ascent and closeness to Allah.
data.etymology: Ilaaf belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Exalted, Sublime.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ilaaf total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

In various Islamic texts and folklore, Ilaaf is an angel or a spiritual guide that helps believers navigate their spiritual journey towards enlightenment and self-improvement. The name is also used in Sufism, the mystical branch of Islam, to describe the ultimate state of union with the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: Ilaaf holds immense spiritual significance for Muslims as it embodies the idea of striving for spiritual growth and closeness to Allah. Through various spiritual practices and acts of worship, Muslims seek to ascend to a higher spiritual plane and attain the presence of Allah. The name Ilaaf serves as a constant reminder of this eternal quest for self-improvement and divine closeness. In surah Ar-Robbiya, Allah Almighty says "Whoever desires the Hereafter, and We will give him an increase.” (Ad-Dhaariyaat: 54) This verse emphasizes the importance of striving for the Hereafter and the constant effort to seek Allah's pleasure, symbolically represented by the name Ilaaf.
